body:
I have recently discovered that the eORCA0.25 and the eORCA0.083 grids (1/4 and 1/12 degree resolution) have a T-Pivot rather than a U-Pivot, i.e. they pivot on tracer points rather than u-velocity points.

Supporting a TPivot is actually extremely easy because it reuses all the machinery we already have for the u-pivot (also for distributed!). Therefore, this PR separates the "topology" from the "pivot", so that RightCenterFolded that is true both for a U and a T pivot can support both.
title: Introducing a TPivot for the tripolar grid

body:
Fixes #6071.

The velocity predictor can leave a nonzero value on an immersed face. The vertically implicit solve then uses that value as a boundary value, even though the immersed velocity must be zero.

Mask each velocity after its predictor step and before the implicit solve. The shared step handles both AB2 and RK3. The existing pressure-correction mask stays in place.

The new regression compares the implicit `w` solve with an independent tridiagonal backward-Euler calculation. It covers vertical forcing and tilted-axis Coriolis at two diffusion factors. A one-step test also checks that forcing inside the immersed region cannot change wet velocities for AB2 or RK3.

On the unchanged base, the first active face differs from the discrete reference: 0.03849084 versus 0.00999438 with forcing, and 0.01714211 versus 0.00706709 with Coriolis. With this change, the focused CPU test passes all 22 checks:

The test ran with Julia 1.12.7 in a local package environment using `Pkg.test("Oceananigans"; test_args=["time_stepping/immersed_vertical_implicit_velocity", "--jobs=1"], coverage=false)`. The full suite, GPU execution, and performance were not tested locally.

Codex used.
title: fix: mask immersed velocities before implicit solve

Our default scheme for `WENOVectorInvariant` is dissipative in the vorticity flux. This PR introduces an energy-conserving version of the same flux, which dissipates enstrophy.
